mood.summary: Fear is still running high. On Nov 5 the S&P 500 fell 4.4% and the Nasdaq slid into a correction, the worst day since April 2025, on worries that election results will slow AI and data-centre spending. The Fear & Greed index sits in Extreme Fear at 20, and bearish individual investors outnumber bulls by about 14 points. Stocks are bouncing on Nov 6 after a strong jobs report (165,000 jobs vs about 60,000 expected), but that also firmed bets on a December Fed rate hike.

trending.note: Board as of Friday 4:08 PM ET; prices are the 2026-11-13 close. Why-it's-trending notes summarize the Stocktwits stream and the news it links to.

items.name: SELLAS Life Sciences Group Inc
items.about: Clinical-stage biotech developing galinpepimut-S, a WT1-targeted cancer vaccine for acute myeloid leukemia.
items.why: SELLAS says topline results from its Phase 3 REGAL trial are due in November after the 80th-event trigger on Oct 28, so traders are positioning ahead of the readout; posts say it could come as soon as Monday. The stock slid about 2% after fading from a $9 high.

items.name: Unity Software Inc
items.about: Makes the Unity engine and ad tools that developers use to build and monetize games and 3D apps.
items.why: Unity rose 5.3% as buyout chatter continued after reports that Silver Lake and Saudi Arabia's PIF held early takeover talks valuing it near $25 billion, with Unity hiring a bank to weigh options. No deal has been announced; posts also cite heavy call buying and a strong earnings beat.

items.name: Viking Therapeutics Inc
items.about: Biotech developing GLP-1 based obesity treatments, including injectable and oral VK2735.
items.why: Viking jumped about 6% with a late surge into the close, tied to a Betaville-flagged takeover rumor that named no buyer. Posts debate whether a deal could come before Phase 3 data; nothing has been confirmed by the company.

items.name: Summit Therapeutics Inc
items.about: Biotech developing ivonescimab, a PD-1/VEGF bispecific antibody for lung cancer.
items.why: The FDA's PDUFA goal date for ivonescimab plus chemo in EGFR-mutated lung cancer is Nov 14, based on the HARMONi Phase 3 trial. Shares fell 6.2% into the decision as some posts flagged rejection risk while others positioned for approval.

items.name: NVIDIA Corp
items.about: Designs the GPUs and networking systems that power most AI data centers.
items.why: Nvidia fell another 2% after Jensen Huang's Nov 12 resignation, leaving it down roughly 12% for the week and below a $4 trillion market value. A broad chip selloff (AMD about -9%) added pressure, and earnings follow on Nov 17 under interim CEO Colette Kress.

items.name: Novo Nordisk A/S
items.about: Danish drugmaker behind the diabetes and obesity drugs Ozempic and Wegovy.
items.why: Novo rose about 2.4% in a quiet session; posts link the move to the Viking takeover rumor, naming Novo as a possible acquirer, which is unconfirmed. Earlier this month Novo raised its 2026 outlook with Q3 results.

items.name: Zevra Therapeutics Inc
items.about: Rare-disease drugmaker whose Miplyffa (arimoclomol) treats Niemann-Pick disease type C.
items.why: Zevra fell about 19% after the EMA's CHMP gave a negative opinion on arimoclomol for Niemann-Pick type C; the European Commission's final decision is due within about 67 days. BTIG cut its target to $21 from $24 but kept a Buy rating.

items.name: Newsmax Inc
items.about: Conservative cable news network and streaming media company.
items.why: Newsmax jumped 31% after Q3 revenue rose 52.5% to $69.0 million with EPS of $0.12, beating estimates. About $14 million of revenue was a one-time termination payment; excluding it, revenue grew 21.6%.

items.name: iShares 20+ Year Treasury Bond ETF
items.about: ETF holding long-dated US Treasury bonds; it falls when long-term yields rise.
items.why: TLT slipped 0.4% as the 10-yr yield rose to about 5.1% after October producer prices showed inflation broadening. Posts also traded late reports of an FAA nationwide ground stop.

items.name: HawkEye 360 Inc.
items.about: Operates satellites that detect and geolocate radio-frequency signals for defense and intelligence customers.
items.why: HawkEye 360 rose 24% after Q3 revenue grew 84% to $59.3 million and it raised 2026 revenue guidance to $225–227 million. Posts highlight comments about counter-drone use cases from the earnings call.

items.name: Rivian Automotive Inc
items.about: Makes electric pickups, SUVs and delivery vans.
items.why: Rivian fell about 4.8%, extending a slide from near $13.70 earlier in the week toward its 12-month low of about $11.38. No company news was found; posts point to weakness across EV stocks.

items.name: Candel Therapeutics Inc
items.about: Biotech developing viral immunotherapies, led by aglatimagene for prostate cancer.
items.why: Candel fell 26% after pushing its prostate cancer BLA to mid-2027 from year-end 2026, citing assay refinement work. Stifel cut its target to $19 from $22; posts also question a reported share-sale facility.

items.name: Backblaze Inc
items.about: Provides low-cost cloud storage and backup services.
items.why: Backblaze fell about 12% with no company announcement found. Posts point to selling across cloud and data-center names; Needham cut its target to $15 from $23 on Nov 3.

items.name: Intuitive Machines Inc
items.about: Builds lunar landers and space infrastructure and provides NASA data-relay services.
items.why: Intuitive Machines swung between $12.03 and $13.47 before closing nearly flat. Posts focus on options expiry and sector news, including a Rocket Lab delay to its first commercial Delta-class flight.

items.name: Vir Biotechnology Inc
items.about: Biotech developing treatments for hepatitis delta and T-cell engager cancer drugs.
items.why: Vir fell about 18% after pricing 15 million shares at $10 to raise $150 million, below the prior $12.12 close. The raise came days after its hepatitis delta drug met the main goal of a Phase 3 trial.

items.name: Klarna Group plc
items.about: Buy-now-pay-later payments and shopping app.
items.why: Klarna rose 8.7% ahead of its Nov 17 earnings, a day after naming Robinhood executive Chris Koegel as incoming CFO. Posts speculate about a takeover, which is unconfirmed.

items.name: Modine Manufacturing Co.
items.about: Makes thermal-management and cooling systems, including liquid cooling for AI data centers.
items.why: Modine jumped about 28% after Bloomberg reported Samsung Electronics is in talks to acquire it; neither company has confirmed a deal. Its data-center sales rose 95% last quarter, and an investor day is set for Nov 18.

items.name: Nebius Group N.V.
items.about: Runs GPU cloud data centers that rent AI computing capacity.
items.why: Nebius fell about 10% for a second day after guiding Q4 to the low end because of data-center delays and raising capex plans, even though Q3 revenue of $981 million beat estimates. Baird, BofA and others cut targets, and the Nvidia CEO exit hit AI-cloud peers.

items.name: Nu Holdings Ltd
items.about: Digital bank serving customers in Brazil, Mexico and Colombia.
items.why: Nu rose 11.7% after record Q3 net income of $1.1 billion (+31%) and revenue of $5.82 billion that beat estimates. The results eased Brazil worries, although 90-day delinquencies rose to 7.3%.

items.name: Netlist Inc
items.about: Makes memory modules and pursues patent cases against large memory chipmakers.
items.why: Netlist fell about 12%, extending losses after a Q3 EPS miss ($0.22 vs $0.60 expected). Posts cite unfavorable news on its '912 patent; that was not confirmed by a news search.
